title: Learning long-term dependencies with gradient descent is difficult
relevance: Classical explanation of why learning distant dependencies is difficult.
novelty_threat: Long-horizon failure and gradient decay are established phenomena, not sufficient novelty.
evidence_locator: Original-paper first-page search extract and indexed abstract; publisher access blocked.
limitations: Optimization difficulty is not a theorem that a competent fixed-weight network must forget under repeated inference.
version_note: Institutional teaching copy of the author manuscript (title page says to appear); publication metadata refers to the final 1994 article.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
relevance: Introduces gated access to a persistent internal memory path and long-delay artificial tasks.
novelty_threat: Gating, persistent state, and delayed cue retention are foundational prior art.
evidence_locator: Author-hosted PDF, pp. 1–2, introduction and architectural motivation; relevant introductory sections inspected.
limitations: Original architecture and learning algorithm differ from modern forget-gate LSTMs; retention depends on the learned complete state.

title: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks
venue: ICML; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 28(3):1310–1318
relevance: Separates numerical and optimization obstacles associated with recurrent gradient propagation.
novelty_threat: A collapse experiment must distinguish failed learning from inference-time loss in a trained competent model.
evidence_locator: Official PMLR abstract and publication metadata.
limitations: Gradient clipping and optimization findings do not establish periodic-driver-specific memory loss.

title: Unitary Evolution Recurrent Neural Networks
venue: ICML; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 48
relevance: A principled long-memory architecture control based on unitary recurrent weights.
novelty_threat: Orthogonal/unitary memory preservation is established; including such models is a control, not a mechanism claim.
evidence_locator: Official PMLR abstract and arXiv metadata.
limitations: A unitary weight matrix alone does not make the entire nonlinear recurrent-state Jacobian unitary.

title: Recurrent Orthogonal Networks and Long-Memory Tasks
venue: ICML; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 48:2034–2042
relevance: Constructs an orthogonal rotational solution to delayed copying and contrasts it with an adding task.
novelty_threat: Cue–delay–query tasks and periodic internal clocks already have analytical recurrent solutions.
evidence_locator: Official PDF, section 3.1, pp. 3–4; copying construction and comparison with adding.
limitations: Blank-delay copying does not test the proposed structured periodic versus matched varying-driver intervention.

title: Opening the Black Box: Low-Dimensional Dynamics in High-Dimensional Recurrent Neural Networks
relevance: Uses fixed and slow points to explain computations in trained high-dimensional networks.
novelty_threat: Low-dimensional dynamics can implement useful memory and computation; low geometry is not inherently pathological.
evidence_locator: Author-institution publication abstract and bibliographic record.
limitations: Only abstract inspected here; detailed dynamical analyses require full-text verification before reuse.

title: Memory traces in dynamical systems
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 105(48):18970–18975
relevance: Measures retained input information relative to noise with a Fisher memory curve.
novelty_threat: Noise-aware dynamical memory measures and normal/nonnormal distinctions long predate participation-ratio comparisons.
evidence_locator: PubMed abstract, PMID 19020074; author PDF introductory extract. Full derivations not audited because later PDF retrieval timed out.
limitations: Memory-capacity bounds depend on stated models and normalization; do not transfer them wholesale to gated task-specific memory.

title: Short-term memory in neuronal networks through dynamical compressed sensing
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 23
relevance: Sparse signal structure allows memory reconstruction beyond a naive neuron-count bound.
novelty_threat: Dimension reduction can preserve reconstructible structured memory; storage dimension is not an unconditional capacity proxy.
evidence_locator: Official NeurIPS abstract, including sparsity and orthogonal-network qualifications.
limitations: Sparse-sequence reconstruction uses assumptions different from smoothly storing independent continuous tags.

title: Information Processing Capacity of Dynamical Systems
relevance: Defines target-function capacities and a qualified total-capacity relation to independent state variables.
novelty_threat: Task-aligned capacity, state dimension, and computation/memory tradeoffs have an established quantitative framework.
evidence_locator: PMC full text, definitions of capacity, orthogonal target functions, and maximum-capacity discussion.
limitations: Bounds rely on target/input assumptions and linear readouts; covariance participation ratio is not their capacity.

title: Trained recurrent neural networks develop phase-locked limit cycles in a working memory task
relevance: Transient cue identities select stable phase-locked memory cycles in a periodically driven trained RNN.
novelty_threat: Direct counterexample to interpreting local contraction or repeated forcing as inevitable categorical forgetting.
evidence_locator: Results, Figs. 1–3; Fig. 3 stable memory cycles; Methods Poincare maps and linear stability analysis; frequency/amplitude manipulation.
limitations: Two cue identities and oscillator-driven output; not the proposed higher-dimensional matched-driver query task. Published middle initial retained without inventing its expansion.

title: Transitions in echo index and dependence on input repetitions
venue: arXiv preprint; published venue not verified in this audit
relevance: Relates symbol dwell/repetition constraints to multiplicity of attracting input-driven responses.
novelty_threat: Repetition-induced retention or loss of initial-state distinctions is already an explicit theoretical topic.
evidence_locator: Sections 2.1–2.3, PDF pp. 6–10; Assumption 2.1 and Theorems 2.3–2.4; sections 3.1–3.3, pp. 11–13.
limitations: Theorems impose basin/hyperbolicity conditions; finite-horizon clustering estimates are not task-specific memory measures.

title: Temporal superposition and feature geometry of RNNs under memory demands
relevance: Analyzes delayed recall using age-indexed features, readout geometry, and interference costs.
novelty_threat: Memory-demand-dependent geometry and beneficial removal of obsolete information are already directly analyzed.
evidence_locator: Sections 3–3.4, pp. 3–5; section 4.1, pp. 5–6; Appendix I.2 for untied-readout qualification.
limitations: Specified recall/input models, including temporally independent inputs in the loss decomposition; does not establish the matched periodic-driver contrast. Unverified middle-name expansions retained as published initials.

title: How Temporal Correlations Shape Memory in Linear Recurrent Neural Networks
relevance: Studies gradient-flow learning and memory/shortcut tradeoffs with stationary temporally correlated inputs.
novelty_threat: Temporal correlations changing learned recurrence and memory cost are current explicit prior art.
evidence_locator: HTML v1 Mathematical Setup and Findings; Appendix C, step 6, lag-one boundary derivation.
limitations: Whitened feature covariance, aligned singular modes, geometric target profiles and linear learning dynamics; the local boundary result does not eliminate all higher-lag effects.

title: Sudden restructuring of memory representations in recurrent neural networks with repeated stimulus presentations
relevance: Repeated presentations alter basin organization and memory representations in a binary recurrent network.
novelty_threat: A title-level repetition/restructuring claim overlaps, but the causal setting differs materially.
evidence_locator: Publisher full text, Methods: Hebbian training, 10-neuron model, enumeration of 1024 states and repeated presentations.
limitations: Weights change during repeated training; this is not fixed-weight inference-time periodic forgetting. Published middle initial not expanded without verification.

title: How noise affects memory in linear recurrent networks
relevance: Derives memory effects of noise spectra and injection structure in linear recurrent systems.
novelty_threat: Noise-resolved memory geometry is established; equal raw noise amplitude need not mean equal memory impairment.
evidence_locator: Main paper pp. 1–2, linear ESN and memory-function definitions; covariance derivation and large-dimension noise-spectrum discussion.
limitations: Assumptions include independent signal/noise and shared injection weights; asymptotic claims are not universal finite-state or gated-network guarantees.

title: A diverse range of factors affect the nature of neural representations underlying short-term memory
relevance: Memory representation form varies with task and circuit factors.
novelty_threat: Observed dynamics or apparent coding differences alone do not establish memory absence.
evidence_locator: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record; cookie barrier prevented final full-text retrieval.
limitations: No detailed methods or theorem claims audited here. Author's published initial retained without speculative expansion.
version_note: Author-hosted published PDF marked Corrected: Publisher Correction.

title: On the Practical Computational Power of Finite Precision RNNs for Language Recognition
relevance: Studies practical numerical restrictions and differences between gated recurrent families.
novelty_threat: Categorical capacity and architecture differences cannot be inferred from differentiable dimension arguments alone.
evidence_locator: Official ACL Anthology abstract, author list, DOI and publication metadata.
limitations: Formal precision/range assumptions must be read before applying results to bounded FP32 state; no hardware-capacity theorem asserted here.

title: On the Computational Power of RNNs
relevance: Shows why numerical assumptions matter in comparisons of recurrent computational power.
novelty_threat: Infinite-real and finite-state memory claims describe different resources and must not be mixed.
evidence_locator: Primary arXiv abstract and author metadata.
limitations: Detailed definitions were not audited; do not treat differences from Weiss et al. as a contradiction without aligning precision models.

title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
relevance: Uses control tasks to distinguish representation evidence from probe capacity.
novelty_threat: High decoding accuracy alone is not an uncontested representation interpretation.
evidence_locator: Official ACL Anthology abstract and metadata.
limitations: Linguistic probing setting; adapt controls to randomized independent memory tags and held-out cue histories.

title: Probing the Probing Paradigm: Does Probing Accuracy Entail Task Relevance?
relevance: Controlled experiments separate decodability from information relevant to task decisions.
novelty_threat: Probe recovery of tags is not evidence that the trained model uses them.
evidence_locator: Official ACL Anthology abstract and publication record; primary arXiv metadata.
limitations: Causal use requires additional interventions; state swaps establish a stronger but still intervention-specific claim.

title: Learning dynamics in linear recurrent neural networks
venue: ICML; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267:49860–49902
relevance: Analyzes learning dynamics, temporal structure, and recurrence/feedthrough tradeoffs.
novelty_threat: Differences in acquired recurrence or learned memory are already studied separately from inference trajectories.
evidence_locator: Official PMLR abstract and complete author metadata.
limitations: Linear learning setting; relevance to fixed-weight nonlinear matched-driver effects requires a separate derivation. Published initials preserved where expansion unverified.
